analysis: The code snippet defines a method resize(int newSize) that creates a new backing array of the specified size and copies elements from the current array. The call to System.arraycopy uses src=(this.items), srcPos=0, dest=(newItems), destPos=0, length=Math.min(size, newItems.length). The 'items' field is non-null and the new array is created via ArrayReflection.newInstance, so both arrays are non-null, avoiding NullPointerException. The arrays have identical component types (obtained via items.getClass().getComponentType()), so ArrayStoreException due to type mismatch between arrays or element conversion is avoided as well, because elements are of the same type. However, IndexOutOfBoundsException can occur if the 'length' argument is negative. In this code, length = Math.min(size, newSize). If newSize is negative, then Math.min(size, negative) yields a negative length, which triggers an IndexOutOfBoundsException. The code does not validate that newSize is non-negative, so this exception is not avoided.
answer: NullPointerException: avoided (both arrays are non-null). ArrayStoreException: avoided (arrays have the same component type). IndexOutOfBoundsException: not avoided (negative newSize leads to negative length).
remark: IndexOutOfBoundsException can be thrown if the 'newSize' parameter is negative because Math.min(size, newSize) would produce a negative length, which violates the precondition that the length argument must be non-negative.
